verdict.rationale: The core self-hosted stack is evidenced. Grafana is open source on GitHub. Mimir is documented as horizontally scalable, highly available, multi-tenant storage with a monolithic mode. Loki's architecture (label-only indexing, chunks in S3/GCS or the local filesystem) and its migrate/upgrade guidance are documented, and Tempo supports open tracing protocols. Community reports note real friction: the stack has grown into many services, and upgrading from Grafana 7 left 'legacy alerts'. Missing for 10: documented upgrade paths for Grafana, Mimir and Tempo (only Loki's is evidenced), end-to-end production architecture docs for the whole stack, self-hosted equivalents of Cloud-documented features such as SLO and incident/on-call, and independent hands-on reports of running the full stack in production.
